newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin fine, advisors plan comeback - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin fine, advisors plan comeback - spokesman.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is recovering well after heart surgery and his aides are looking for the best time to stage his first appearence since his operation, the presidential press secretary said on Friday.
"All indicators are stable. His movements are being expanded," Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a news briefing.
He said a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act after multiple bypass surgery on November 5, was still being prepared but did not say when it would be.
Yastrzhembsky said on Tuesday that Yeltsin would address the nation within days, but did not specify whether it would be on television or radio.
On Friday he said no timetable for an address had been set but added that this had nothing to do with the president's state of health.
"You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact," he said.
Yastrzhembsky gave no indication as to when would be the right time for Yeltsin to appear.

He said that doctors, generally encouraged by the smooth progress made by the 65-year-old president, still wanted Yeltsin to build up his work-day step by step to avoid the risk of long-term damage to his health if he proceeds too quickly.
"The doctors favour progress achieved in small steps," Yastzhembsky said.
"In the near future there are no meetings planned in his schedule," he said.

Pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who was a consultant during the operation, has said Yeltsin had good chances for unlimited activity in the next 10 or 15 years but cautioned the president not to try to go too fast.
